events.text: The headman of Pear Blossom Village comes up the hill road on foot, with two boys carrying a basket of rice, a smoked duck and a purse. 'For your kindness in leaving us be,' he says, and will not lift his eyes. Nobody asked them to pay. Fear asked them.

choices.text: Take it, and name a yearly sum

effects.log: You name a yearly sum. The headman bows lower than before and goes down the hill without the purse. (+60 taels)

choices.text: Keep the duck, send the silver back

effects.log: You keep the duck and send the purse home. The village does not know what to make of it, and argues about it for a month.

choices.text: Send it all back and tell them never to come

effects.log: You send the basket back untouched. The headman goes down the hill looking more frightened than when he came.

events.text: Smoke over Pear Blossom: the Red Turban bandits have come down from the ridge, and they want the same tribute the village pays you. The headman is at your door again, this time on his knees. 'They say they are not afraid of you,' he says, as if that settles it.

choices.text: Ride down and drive them off

ok.log: The fight is short. The Red Turbans run for the ridge and the village lights every lantern it owns.

fail.log: You drive them off, but the chief catches you with the butt of a spear before he runs. You limp home to a basket of eggs.

choices.text: Tell the bandits the village is yours, and take a cut from them too

effects.log: The bandits pay you to look away, and the village pays you as well. Everyone is poorer except you. (+80 taels)
You shut the door. By morning the bandits have taken the granary, and your name means a little less in the valley.

events.text: Years of tribute have emptied Pear Blossom. Half the houses stand shut, and the ones still lit hide their rice under the floor. This spring the purse is light, and the headman, older now, brings his granddaughter to plead for the village instead.

effects.log: You snap the tally sticks over your knee. The girl stares at you as if you had grown a second head.
They pay. The next year there is nobody left in the village to pay anything. (+50 taels)

choices.text: Take the village's best fields instead

effects.log: The fields are yours now, and the families who farmed them farm them for you. (+120 taels)

events.text: Pear Blossom has grown used to you. The children leave peaches on the wall of the hill house, and the headman, who still bows too low, has carved your name on the shrine to the earth god, between the god and the well. It is the strangest honour you have had.

effects.log: Your name stays on the shrine. Travellers ask about it, and the village tells them a version of you that is kinder than the truth.

choices.text: Ask them to scratch it off

effects.log: They scratch it off, very carefully, and carve a pear blossom in its place. Everyone still knows whose it is.

choices.text: Use the village as a hideout from now on

effects.log: Pear Blossom keeps your secrets. Hunters who ask about you are given tea and wrong directions.

events.text: A boy of nine with a charcoal moustache and a black rag tied over his face is robbing the other children of their sweet buns in the lane below the inn. 'I am you,' he announces when he sees you, delighted. His name is Little Pang, and your wanted poster hangs above his bed.

effects.log: You fix his stance and his grip. He runs off to rob the buns properly, and the lane has a new terror.

choices.text: Tell him the truth about the road

effects.log: You tell him what it costs: the cold inns, the posters, the friends who stop writing. He listens with his mouth open, unconvinced.

choices.text: Make him give the buns back

effects.log: He gives them back, sulking. The other children look at you as if you were the magistrate.

events.text: Little Pang is twelve now, and turns up at your door with a bundle and a wooden sword. His mother, a candle-seller called Widow Pang, is behind him with a broom. 'Take me,' says the boy. 'Take him,' says the widow, 'and I will find you.'

choices.text: Take him on as a runner

effects.log: He runs messages faster than anyone you have had. The widow throws the broom after you both. (+20 taels)
You send him home with his sword over his shoulder. He does not speak to you for a year.

choices.text: Give the widow silver for his schooling

effects.log: The widow takes it without a word and drags the boy off by the ear to the schoolmaster. (-50 taels)

events.text: Pang is grown, faster than you were and colder. He has started taking jobs you would have turned down, and last week he burned a granary to make a point you never asked him to make. The widow sends no more brooms. She sends nothing.

effects.log: He goes without arguing. Within a year his own poster is up beside yours, with a higher price.

choices.text: Make him your heir in the trade

effects.log: You give him the routes, the fences and the names. The murim now has two of you, and the second is worse.

choices.text: Make him rebuild the granary with you

ok.log: He sulks for a week and then works like an ox. When the roof is on, he stands under it a long time and says nothing.

fail.log: He laughs in your face and leaves. You build the granary alone, and the county watches.

events.text: A young constable with a straight back stops you at the river gate and looks at your papers for a long time. It is Pang. 'I read every poster,' he says quietly. 'That was how I learned what a constable is for.' He hands the papers back. 'Not today. Go.'

effects.log: You go through the gate. When you look back, he is already checking the next cart, very properly.
He does it with shaking hands. At the yamen the widow is waiting with a basket of candles, for the cell.

choices.text: Slip him silver for the widow

effects.log: He refuses it twice and takes it the third time, for her. (-30 taels)

events.text: A sedan chair stops outside the inn and a stout merchant in grey silk climbs out. You know the face a moment before he says it: Merchant Qiao, whose silk convoy you emptied on the Hanzhong road years ago. 'I started again with one mule,' he says. 'I have forty now. Sit with me.'

effects.log: He pours. He talks about mules for an hour. He does not mention the silk once, which is worse than if he had.
You are out of the back door before the tea comes. Qiao tells the whole inn that you ran from a silk merchant.
'Nothing you can give back,' he says. 'Something you can do.' He smiles like a man holding the better hand.

events.text: Qiao wants nothing back. He wants you to guard his forty mules through the Qinling passes, where the bandits are worse than you ever were. 'Who better?' he says. 'You know every place a convoy can be robbed.' The pay is good. The joke is not lost on anyone.

ok.log: Not a mule is lost. Qiao pays in full and laughs all the way to Chengdu. (+150 taels)

fail.log: Bandits hit the rear of the train and you lose three mules and some skin. Qiao pays you anyway. (+40 taels)

choices.text: Rob him again, for old times

effects.log: At the narrowest pass you take the whole train. Qiao does not shout. He just sits down in the road. (+200 taels)
'I thought not,' Qiao says, and hires a dozen guards who are worse than you would have been.

events.text: A letter from Qiao, written in his big careless hand: his daughter is marrying, and there is a seat at the high table for the bandit who once took everything and then brought it back over the mountains. 'Come in your own name,' it says. 'Let them stare.'

effects.log: They stare. Qiao makes a toast to second chances and does not say whose. The bride laughs.
You sit at the high table as a distant cousin from Xi'an. Qiao winks at you all evening.
A bolt of red brocade, unsigned. Qiao knows at once and keeps the wrapping. (-60 taels)

events.text: Qiao does not start again this time. You hear it in a teahouse: the forty mules sold, the warehouses shut, the merchant sitting by the river with a fishing pole he never casts. The teahouse has a name for what you did to him. It is not a kind one.

choices.text: Send back half the silver, unsigned

effects.log: The silver arrives in a rice sack. Qiao buys one mule with it, and then another. (-100 taels)
You shrug. The teahouse name for you spreads to two more towns.

choices.text: Go and sit with him at the river

ok.log: He lets you sit. He does not forgive you, but he lets you sit, and after an hour he casts the line.

fail.log: He throws the fishing pole at you and walks home. The whole riverbank saw.

events.text: The new wanted poster at the Xiangyang gate has your name, a reward of 300 taels, and a portrait of someone with a face like a worried turnip, a beard you never had and one ear much larger than the other. Two guards are studying it. They look straight at you and see nothing.

effects.log: You walk under your own poster and buy a pear on the other side. The guards are still arguing about the ear.

ok.log: The painter is so grateful for the sitting that he paints a second, very good one. It goes up all over the county.

fail.log: The painter tells you the portrait is perfect and that you are the one who looks wrong.

choices.text: Pull it down and keep it

effects.log: You roll it up and keep it in your sleeve. On bad days you take it out and look at the ear.

events.text: The turnip face has caught someone. Old Liu, a steamed-bun seller with an unlucky ear, is in the Xiangyang lock-up, and the magistrate is writing to the Alliance for the reward. Liu's wife has set up a stall outside the yamen to sell buns and weep, both at once.

choices.text: Walk into the yamen and say who you are

effects.log: The magistrate looks from you to the poster to Liu and back. Liu goes home. You do not, for a year.

ok.log: Liu wakes up in his own bed. The next poster says you rescue bun sellers, and your price goes up.

fail.log: A roof tile slips. You and Liu share a cell for a year, and he talks about dough the entire time.

effects.log: Liu sits in the lock-up for three months before the magistrate admits the ear is wrong.

events.text: Xiangyang has given up on portraits. The new poster reads only: 'A person of ordinary height with a face you would not remember. Reward 500 taels.' Half the city has been reported by the other half. The magistrate has started hiding from his own constables.

effects.log: The constables arrest their own magistrate on an anonymous tip. The city laughs about it for a month.

choices.text: Buy buns at the yamen gate

effects.log: The Lius' stall is doing well. Mrs Liu gives you two for one and says you have an honest face.
The painter weeps with gratitude. By spring your real face is on every gate in Hubei.

events.text: Blind Storyteller Hu sits in the corner of the Plum Rain teahouse with a fan and a wooden clapper, and for 40 taels he will tell the city whatever you like about yourself. 'Worse sells better,' he says. 'But better is cheaper to believe.'

choices.text: Pay him to make you worse

effects.log: Hu takes the silver and smiles a very wide smile. (-40 taels)

choices.text: Pay him to make you better

effects.log: Hu takes the silver and sighs. Kind stories are harder work. (-40 taels)

choices.text: Tell him to leave you out of it

effects.log: He shrugs. 'Then I will make it up myself,' he says, and clacks the clapper twice.

events.text: Hu has outdone himself. In his telling you drank a lake dry at Dongting, ate an orthodox elder's horse whole and frightened a typhoon back out to sea. Bounty hunters from three provinces have heard it. Some of them are now very nervous. Some are very interested.

roll.foeName: a hunter who believed none of it

ok.log: The hunter goes home on a door, and Hu adds a fourth wonder to the story.

fail.log: The hunter was not frightened at all. You get away, but the story gets a new ending.

choices.text: Pay Hu to tone it down

effects.log: Hu cuts the horse but keeps the typhoon. (-20 taels)
Nobody dares sit at your table in any teahouse. You eat in peace for a whole year.

events.text: Hu's kinder story has spread: you robbed only the rich, fed the poor, and once carried a grandmother across a flood. Now a grandmother is at your door, a flood is coming down the Han, and the whole street is watching to see if the story is true.

ok.log: You carry her across on your back. Hu adds it to the story that evening, and for once does not have to make anything up.

fail.log: You get her across, but the current nearly takes you both. She hits you with her cane for it.

choices.text: Pay a boatman to do it

effects.log: The boatman takes her. The street decides the story was exaggerated. (-30 taels)
You go out by the back. The grandmother is carried by a cobbler, who gets the story instead.

events.text: Hu kept his word in his own way. His new story is about a villain whose name nobody knows, who robbed an emperor's barge and was never seen again. It is the most famous story in the city, and it is about you, and nobody knows it.

choices.text: Tell him the ending he got wrong

effects.log: He listens, nods, and changes nothing. The next night the story is better than the truth.

choices.text: Pay him to keep it nameless forever

effects.log: He bites the silver and promises. He is the most honest liar in the city. (-30 taels)
You sit at the back and listen to yourself. It is a very good story.

events.text: The hunters are two valleys behind you when you reach the gate of Cold Spring Monastery. The abbot, a small old monk called Huiming, looks at the dust on your boots and the blade under your coat. 'We need someone to carry water,' he says. 'Shave your head and start tonight.'

effects.log: The razor is cold and the buckets are heavy. By the end of the first week your hands have new calluses in new places.

choices.text: Hide in the woodshed without a word

effects.log: The monks pretend not to see you. Every evening a bowl of rice appears on the chopping block.

choices.text: Threaten the abbot to keep him quiet

effects.log: Huiming listens to the threat politely and says, 'Yes, yes. The water is still not going to carry itself.'

events.text: A band of Alliance hunters climbs the monastery steps at dawn, led by a hard-faced swordswoman called Iron Lotus Ma. 'We are looking for a killer,' she tells Huiming. Behind the abbot, among the novices sweeping the yard, you keep your eyes on the broom.

ok.log: Ma looks at every face twice, yours too, and goes back down the mountain. The broom keeps moving.

fail.log: Ma knows your walk. You go over the back wall and do not stop running until the western hills.

choices.text: Step out so the monks are not blamed

ok.log: You meet her outside the gate, beat her fairly, and send her down the mountain. The monks pretend they saw nothing.

fail.log: She wins. The monks watch you led away in chains, and they pray for you every morning.

choices.text: Let the abbot lie for you

effects.log: Huiming looks Ma in the eye and says there is no stranger here. It is the first lie he has told in forty years.

events.text: Huiming is dying, slowly and cheerfully, in a cell that smells of pine. He asks you to sit. 'You carried more water than any novice I have had,' he says. 'Stay and take the vows, or go back down. Either is a road. Only choose it.'

effects.log: You kneel in the hall with the novices half your age. Huiming dies that night, smiling, with the bell still ringing.
You leave with a shaved head and nothing else, and find that your breathing is quieter than it was.
He talks until dawn about water, breath and very old mistakes. You remember every word.

events.text: Two years on, a letter finds you, carried by a novice who walked for a month: Huiming is dying and asks for the stranger who never took the vows. 'You never carried water,' the letter says, 'but you never quite left either. Come and say goodbye.'

effects.log: You arrive a day before he dies. He asks you to carry one bucket of water, and you do.
You burn the letter. For years afterwards, the sound of a temple bell makes you stop in the road.

events.text: A bounty hunter called Gao Ren has been on your trail for three months: a patient, sunburned woman with a crossbow, a mule called Dumpling and a notebook of everything you have ever eaten. Tonight a storm closes the pass, and the only shelter for ten li is one cave. Gao is already in it.

effects.log: Neither of you sleeps. By morning you know the name of the mule's mother, and she knows your favourite noodles.

ok.log: She loses, ties up her own bruises without a word, and sleeps with the mule at the cave mouth.

fail.log: She wins. You spend the night in the rain, and she writes it in the notebook.

effects.log: You walk all night in the rain. In the morning you are soaked and ahead of her, which is something.

events.text: Gao Ren catches up with you again at a noodle stall in Hanzhong and sits down without asking. 'The Alliance wants you alive. The Wolf Sect wants you dead and pays more,' she says, eating your noodles. 'I want my mule fed. Trade me camps for camps.'

effects.log: You tell her where the Wolf Sect sleeps. She tells you where the Alliance does. Neither of you writes it down.

choices.text: Offer to feed the mule for a year

effects.log: She looks at the silver, then at you, and laughs for the first time. (-40 taels)
She calls you a cheap villain to the whole street, and pays.

events.text: The Wolf Sect has Gao Ren in a cage cart on the north road. She took a job against them on your word, and the word was good, but they were more. Her mule, Dumpling, found you on its own and is standing outside the inn, waiting.

ok.log: The escort breaks. Gao climbs out of the cage, looks at you, and says, "You are late."

fail.log: You get her out, but take a wound in the shoulder that will ache every winter.

effects.log: The Wolf Sect sells her back for silver, and laughs at you for paying. Gao does not laugh. (-150 taels)
Dumpling follows you for three days, then turns and goes home without you.

events.text: Gao Ren has retired with Dumpling to a pear orchard in Shu. A letter comes every spring, with dried pears and a line that never changes: 'Still not hunting you.' This year there is a second line: 'There is a house at the end of the orchard. Nobody would look there.'

effects.log: The house has a leaking roof and a view of the whole valley. Dumpling bites you on the first day, as a greeting.

choices.text: Write back and stay where you are

effects.log: You write back: 'Still not caught.' It becomes the line you send every spring.

choices.text: Send her the price on your head, as a joke

effects.log: She frames the letter and spends the silver on a new mule. (-50 taels)

events.text: A villain called Smiling Mo, who poisoned the Qingcheng sect's tea and laughed through the trial, sends you a lacquer box. Inside is half a map of the imperial salt depot at Zigong. 'The other half is in my head,' says the note. 'Partners?'

effects.log: You send back the box with a single word inside. Mo replies with a drawing of a smile.

choices.text: Send the box to the Alliance

effects.log: The Alliance thanks you in a very careful letter, and sets a trap at Zigong.
You keep the lacquer box for tea leaves. It is a very good box.

events.text: The night at the Zigong depot goes well until the vault is open, when Smiling Mo's people quietly step between you and the silver. Mo is smiling, as always. 'Partners until here,' Mo says. 'I did warn you about the name.'

ok.log: Mo stops smiling for the first time anyone can remember. You leave with half the silver. (+250 taels)

fail.log: Mo is faster than the stories said. You leave with nothing but the bruises.

choices.text: You had a plan for this

ok.log: The real silver was in the second vault, which you emptied while Mo guarded the first. (+300 taels)

fail.log: Your plan meets the depot guards head on. Mo waves to you as they lead you away.

effects.log: You walk out of the depot. Behind you, Mo laughs until the guards come.

events.text: Smiling Mo turns up on the Alliance's most-wanted list right below you, and above you on the one the teahouses keep. Mo writes again: 'One more job. A real one, this time. I will even let you hold the map.'

effects.log: You leave Mo tied to the depot gate for the guards, still smiling. (+120 taels)

choices.text: Turn Mo in to the Alliance

effects.log: Mo is taken at an inn in Yibin. From the cart, Mo blows you a kiss of pure spite.
The letter burns with a faint smell of almonds. You decide not to wonder why.

events.text: Smiling Mo slipped the Alliance's trap, and knows who set it. A lacquer box arrives: inside, a single teacup and a note. 'Drink with me some time.' The cup smells faintly of almonds. The note smells faintly of nothing at all, which is worse.

effects.log: The cup sinks. Fish die for a li downstream. You change inns.

ok.log: The glaze is laced with a slow poison from Yunnan. Now you know it, and you know Mo.

fail.log: You touch the rim to check, and spend a week sick in bed. Mo sends flowers.

effects.log: You send a cup of your own, perfectly clean. Mo never dares drink from it, which was the point.

events.text: An envoy of the Demonic Cult waits in your room, sitting in the dark with your tea: a tall, courteous figure in plum robes, a black jade token on the table. 'The Heavenly Demon has read about you,' the envoy says. 'The Cult has a seat for people the orthodox world has no use for.'

effects.log: The jade is cold and heavier than it looks. The envoy bows and is gone before the candle flickers.
'One task,' says the envoy. 'Everything has a price. Ours is only honest about it.'
The envoy bows. 'The offer does not expire. Neither do we.'

events.text: The envoy's test arrives in a sealed letter: a magistrate in Kaifeng keeps a list of Cult informers, and the list must burn before the spring. 'Do this,' the letter says, 'and the Cult's doors open. Fail, and nobody will hear of it, including you.'

ok.log: The list burns in the magistrate's study while he sleeps two rooms away. By morning a plum blossom is painted on your door.

fail.log: The yamen guards wake. You flee north with half the list burned and the other half in your head.

effects.log: The magistrate moves the list to a vault and does not ask how you knew.
The spring comes and goes. The envoy's chair in your room stays empty, which is somehow worse.

events.text: The Cult sends a black horse and a robe with plum embroidery, and a place at its western stronghold for whenever you want it. The envoy is there too, smiling. 'Most people are sent,' the envoy says. 'You were invited. In the Cult that is worth more than a manual.'

effects.log: The robe fits perfectly. You do not ask how they knew your measurements.

choices.text: Keep the horse, not the robe

effects.log: The horse is the best you have ever ridden. The envoy takes the robe back without a word.
The Cult does not reply. The horse, oddly, keeps finding its way back to your stable.

events.text: Someone has painted a plum blossom on your door in the night: the Cult's mark for a debt. The magistrate you warned is safe in Kaifeng and has sent no thanks. The envoy, in a dream you are not sure was a dream, says only: 'We remember.'

effects.log: You go south on a grain barge and do not look back. For a year, plum blossoms make you jump.

ok.log: The assassin comes on the third night and leaves without the job done. The Cult sends no more.

fail.log: The assassin is very good. You live, mostly because the assassin was only sent to warn you.

ok.log: The magistrate posts two guards at your door and quietly loses your file.

fail.log: The magistrate does not remember you. His clerk remembers your poster.

events.text: Crow's Throat Pass is four paces wide and the only road from Gansu to the river plains. The fort above it has stood empty since the last war. A handful of hard people and a few barrels of nails could hold it, and then everyone who crosses would know your name.

choices.text: Take the pass and charge a toll

effects.log: Your crew moves into the fort. The first caravan pays without arguing. (+60 taels)

choices.text: Take the pass and charge only names

effects.log: Everyone who crosses must say your name aloud at the gate. Within a year, the whole north knows it.
You ride through like anyone else. The fort stays empty, and the wind sings in it.

events.text: A column of imperial soldiers comes up the road under a yellow banner: grain for the frontier, and a young captain with orders to pass and no orders about you. Behind them, in a long line, wait refugees from a flooded county, carrying everything they own.

effects.log: The captain salutes as he passes. The refugees leave a basket of dried dates at the gate.

choices.text: Charge the soldiers, wave the refugees through

ok.log: The captain pays, red-faced. The refugees cheer you all the way down the pass. (+150 taels)

fail.log: The captain does not pay. He charges. The fight is short and costs you the fort.

effects.log: The refugees turn back to the flood. The soldiers turn back to fetch more soldiers.

events.text: The court has noticed Crow's Throat. A general's letter, stamped red: hold the pass against the northern raiders this autumn and your time at the pass is forgotten. Refuse, and five thousand men will come up the road to take it back.

ok.log: The raiders break on the walls three times and go home. The general writes your name into the dispatch.

fail.log: The pass holds, barely. You are carried down it on a stretcher, pardoned for part of it.

effects.log: You leave the gate open and go west. The five thousand men find only nails.

choices.text: Sell the pass to the raiders

effects.log: The raiders pour through Crow's Throat. Your name goes to the Dragon Throne itself. (+300 taels)

events.text: General Lu's quartermaster meets you in a millet field and sets a heavy purse and a sealed jar on the ground between you. The rebel town of Fenshui has held out a year on its wells. 'Put this in the three wells,' he says. 'Nobody need die. They will only be too sick to hold the gates.'

effects.log: The purse is heavy. The jar is heavier. (+200 taels)
You walk away through the millet. The quartermaster calls after you that someone else will do it.

choices.text: Refuse, and break the jar on a stone

effects.log: The jar breaks. The millet around it turns grey in a day.

events.text: Fenshui at night. The three wells stand in the square, the central one with a little roof and a stone frog the children rub for luck. A gate guard is asleep. The jar is warm in your hands. Nobody would ever know who did it.

effects.log: By morning Fenshui is sick. By noon the gates open. Nobody dies, but nobody forgets the stone frog.

choices.text: Pour it into the moat and keep the silver

effects.log: You tip it into the moat and tell the quartermaster the town must have strong stomachs.

choices.text: Wake the guard and warn the town

effects.log: The guard nearly runs you through, then listens. Fenshui guards its wells day and night after that.

events.text: A woman from Fenshui finds you on the road: a schoolteacher called Ruan with a stone frog in her sleeve. She does not shout. 'Three children never got their strength back,' she says. 'I wanted to see what kind of person it was. Now I have.' She walks on.

effects.log: She takes it for the children and will not say your name aloud. (-100 taels)
She goes. Her words come with you, and stay.

choices.text: Go to Fenshui and work off the debt

effects.log: You carry water for the sick children for a whole season. Ruan never speaks to you. She lets you stay.

events.text: General Lu is not a fool. His quartermaster finds you again, this time with four soldiers. 'The town did not fall sick,' he says. 'The general would like his silver back, and an explanation, in that order.'

effects.log: You count it out into his hands. He counts it twice. (-200 taels)

ok.log: The four soldiers go back to the general with a very short explanation.

fail.log: They beat you and take half the silver from your boots. (-100 taels)

ok.log: The quartermaster, who has a sister in Fenshui, looks at you a long time and lets you go.

fail.log: The truth earns you two years in the general's stockade.

events.text: Fenshui held. When General Lu's army finally gave up and marched south, the town carved a new stone frog for the central well, with a ragged figure kneeling beside it. The teachers tell the children it is a story about a jar.

effects.log: You stand in the square and drink from the well. A child rubs the frog and then, shyly, the kneeling figure.
You never go back. Somewhere a stone version of you kneels in the rain, which is enough.

events.text: At the foot of Mount Song, nine sects have met under one awning: Wudang, Emei, Kunlun, the Beggars' Gang and five more, quarrelling over seating and who pays for the tea. They have agreed on one thing only: a coalition, a joint banner, and your name at the top of it.

ok.log: A forged letter, a stolen seating chart, a rumour about the tea money. By evening Emei and Kunlun are not speaking.

fail.log: They see through it at once, and the banner goes up a day early.

ok.log: You burn the awning and the seating chart. Nine sects now hate you personally.

fail.log: The sentries are awake. You escape with a gash and a story nobody will believe.

effects.log: You go west, over the passes. The banner goes up behind you anyway.

events.text: The coalition's banner is on every road. They have split the country into nine hunting grounds and marked your likely paths in red. One map, taken from a Kunlun courier, shows the trap: a ferry at Yichang, a moonless night, forty swords.

choices.text: Use the map to slip through

ok.log: You cross the river ten li upstream on a fishing boat, while forty swords watch an empty ferry.

fail.log: The map was a second trap. You get away, wet and furious.

choices.text: Send a decoy in your coat

effects.log: The forty swords catch a drunk in your coat, who is delighted by all the attention. They let him go in disgust.

choices.text: Walk to the ferry and talk to them

ok.log: Forty swords and one ferry lantern, and you talk until dawn. Two sects go home without drawing.

fail.log: They listen politely, then take you to the Alliance cells.

events.text: The coalition has dissolved into the usual feud. Wudang accuses Emei of stealing the banner; Kunlun has gone home in a sulk; the Beggars' Gang is selling copies of the seating chart. A Kunlun elder writes: 'Well played. Next time we will not invite Emei.'

effects.log: You send the elder a cordial reply and a box of tea. Kunlun now quietly likes you.

choices.text: Send Emei a gift in Kunlun's name

effects.log: Emei is insulted, as intended. The feud runs for another ten years.
You let the sects forget why they met. It does not take long.

events.text: The coalition sends an elder of Wudang under a white flag. Since the ferry, two of the nine sects will not raise a sword to you, and three more are wavering. 'Swear before the nine banners never to harm a sect disciple again,' says the elder, 'and the coalition dissolves.'

effects.log: You swear under nine banners. The banners come down one by one, and the elders go home to argue about something else.
The elder bows and goes. 'Then we will keep hunting,' he says, 'but more slowly.'

events.text: The Martial Alliance has posted a reward for you: 600 taels, sealed by the Alliance Leader himself, on every teahouse wall from here to Luoyang. Your henchman Big Wu reads it three times, moving his lips, and then looks at you with an expression you do not like.

effects.log: Big Wu takes the raise and stops looking at walls. Mostly. (-60 taels)

choices.text: Joke that you would turn yourself in at that price

effects.log: Big Wu laughs too long and too loudly. It does not make you feel better.
He goes, sulking. You spend a month wondering who he is talking to.

events.text: The reward has gone up to 1,000 taels. Big Wu has been to the post station twice this week, and somebody has been asking the innkeeper about your route north. An idea arrives: what if the one who collects the reward is you?

choices.text: Deliver your own body: a coffin of river stones

ok.log: A clerk of the Alliance pays a first share against the coffin, unopened. (+400 taels)

fail.log: The clerk opens the coffin. You spend two years explaining it.

choices.text: Have it out with Big Wu

ok.log: He breaks down and confesses: he only wanted to buy his mother a roof. He was writing to a roofer.

fail.log: He swings first and runs to the Alliance. You go north before they come.

effects.log: You leave in the night without a word to anyone.

events.text: The Alliance has discovered the coffin was full of river stones. The reward is now 2,000 taels, and the poster adds a new line: 'Also wanted for fraud against the Alliance.' Alliance Leader Zhuge is said to have broken his teacup when he heard.

effects.log: A fine celadon cup, unsigned. Zhuge breaks that one too. (-20 taels)
You disappear for a year. The poster fades. The teacup story does not.
You return it with a note of apology. Zhuge does not break a cup this time. (-400 taels)

events.text: Big Wu has bought his mother a roof after all, with silver you gave him, and she wants to meet the person her son works for. She has made dumplings. She has heard nothing about you but kind things. Big Wu is sweating.

effects.log: You eat forty dumplings and praise the roof. Big Wu looks at you as if you had saved his life.
She listens, then puts more dumplings on your plate. "Everyone was something before," she says.

events.text: Luoyang has shut its nine gates for you. Your face is on every wall, constables search every cart, and Alliance swordsmen watch the wharves. Getting out will take time. You rent a room over a funeral paper shop and decide who to become.

effects.log: You learn to fold paper horses and paper houses. You are not good at it, which makes you very convincing.
You shave, buy a rosary from the shop and learn three sutras badly.

choices.text: Nobody at all: hide in the room

effects.log: You spend weeks in a room the size of a coffin. It is very safe and very bad for the knees.

events.text: Months as someone else. The city has stopped searching carts, but Constable Fei, an old man with a limp and a famous memory, is going door to door on your street with a portrait and a cup of tea at every house. Tomorrow he reaches the paper shop.

ok.log: You sell him a paper horse for his late wife. He thanks you and moves on.

fail.log: Fei looks a moment too long and limps away without a word. He knows. He has not said so.

ok.log: You run the rooftops to the wall and drop into the river. By dawn you are on a barge south.

fail.log: A tile slips. You land in a constable's courtyard, beside the constable.

effects.log: He talks about his grandchildren for an hour and leaves without looking at the portrait.

events.text: The Lantern Festival: the gates stand open for one night, and half the city walks out to the river to float lanterns. Constable Fei stands at the Changxia gate, leaning on his stick, looking at each face as it goes by. You join the crowd.

choices.text: Walk past Fei with your lantern

ok.log: Fei's eyes rest on you for a moment. 'Happy festival,' he says. You are through.

fail.log: Fei puts a hand on your sleeve. 'Happy festival,' he says sadly, and waves the constables over.

choices.text: Carry an old woman's lantern basket and walk with her

ok.log: Fei nods to the grandmother and her helper. You carry the basket all the way to the river, and keep going.

fail.log: The grandmother recognises you from the poster and says so, loudly.

choices.text: Go over the wall away from the crowd

ok.log: You go over the north wall while the city watches the river. Nobody looks up.

fail.log: The wall is higher than it looked, and the guard below it is awake.

events.text: A letter with no name reaches you far from Luoyang: Constable Fei has retired. 'I knew you at the paper shop,' he writes. 'You poured the tea properly. A person who pours tea properly can still do something decent. Go and do it.'

effects.log: You keep it folded in your sleeve. On bad days you take it out and read it.
A pound of the best tea in Jiangnan, unsigned. He would know. (-30 taels)

events.text: You go up into the Taibai mountains in late autumn with the hunters a day behind, and the first snow comes down that night. By morning your tracks are the only marks on the mountain, perfectly clear, leading straight to you. Somewhere below, a horn blows.

choices.text: Walk in the stream to break the trail

effects.log: You walk a li in water so cold it hurts your teeth. The trail ends at the stream, and so does the horn.

choices.text: Lay a false trail to a cliff

ok.log: The hunters follow your tracks to the edge of a cliff and stand there arguing for an hour.

fail.log: They do not fall for it. You lose a day and a glove.

choices.text: Turn and fight them on the ridge

ok.log: The fight in the snow is short. The hunters go down the mountain carrying each other.

fail.log: There are more of them than you counted. They carry you down instead.

events.text: Deep winter. You live in a collapsed charcoal-burner's hut on stolen rice, melted snow and pine-needle tea. Smoke from the hunters' camp rises from the valley every morning. Today a lone figure is climbing toward you: an old herb-gatherer with a basket.

effects.log: He is called Grandfather Tian. He shares his millet, mends your boot and asks no questions at all.
You lie in the snow behind the hut until he passes. Your fingers do not forget it.

choices.text: Take his basket and send him off

effects.log: He gives it up without a word and walks back down. You eat his roots and feel worse.

events.text: The thaw comes. The hunters break camp and go down to look elsewhere. Grandfather Tian climbs up one last time with a bundle of clean clothes and a pass for the valley road. 'They asked me every week,' he says. 'I said the mountain was empty.'

effects.log: You thank him. He waves it away and points at the road.
He weighs it, frowns, and gives half back for the road. (-80 taels)

choices.text: Stay a season and gather herbs with him

effects.log: You learn the names of forty roots and the taste of most of them. The hunters never come back.

events.text: The thaw comes, and with it a thin, hard version of you, walking down out of the Taibai mountains. The hunters are gone. In the valley, a wanted poster has faded to nothing in the snow. Another is being pasted up on top of it.

effects.log: You walk until the air is warm, and sleep for three days in a ferry inn.
The first job after the winter pays well. You were hungry for it. (+40 taels)

events.text: A eunuch of the Inner Court arrives in a closed sedan with an escort of twelve and an edict wrapped in yellow silk. The Dragon Throne has a war on the coast, pirates in forty ships, and a shortage of people who frighten things. 'Serve three years,' the eunuch says, 'and walk away pardoned.'

effects.log: You ride south with the escort. The sea smells of salt, tar and other people's war.

ok.log: The eunuch sighs and adds a year's wages in advance. (+100 taels)

fail.log: The eunuch reminds you who is being pardoned. You go anyway.

effects.log: The eunuch rolls up the edict. 'The Throne remembers refusals,' he says, and climbs back into the sedan.

events.text: The pirate fleet lies at anchor behind the Zhoushan islands. The admiral, a careful old man called Qi, wants someone to slip into their anchorage and fire the powder ship. 'If you fail, I never met you,' he says. 'If you succeed, I still never met you, but I will mention you.'

ok.log: The powder ship goes up like the end of the world. The pirate fleet scatters by morning.

fail.log: The fuse is damp. You swim back half-drowned, but Admiral Qi sends the fleet in anyway and wins.

ok.log: You take the flagship. The pirate captain surrenders to you personally, which annoys the admiral.

fail.log: The boarding fails. You serve out the rest of your years in the galley, cooking for the navy.

choices.text: Desert and sell the plan to the pirates

effects.log: The pirates pay well and sail away early. (+250 taels)

events.text: The three years are up. Admiral Qi signs a memorial to the Throne, and the eunuch comes back in the same closed sedan with a second edict in yellow silk. Your crimes are pardoned. Some names on the Alliance's list are not happy about it.

choices.text: Take the pardon and go home quietly

effects.log: You take the silk and go. For the first time in years, you sleep facing the window.
Admiral Qi gives you a ship and a crew of former smugglers. They are very good. (+100 taels)

choices.text: Throw the edict into the sea

effects.log: The eunuch watches the yellow silk drift away on the tide, and says nothing at all.

events.text: The pirates were beaten anyway, and the ones you sold the plan to were the first caught. Now both the Throne and the pirate survivors want you. The eunuch's new poster carries a seal you have never seen before, and the price is in gold.

effects.log: You go so far west the posters are in a different script.

choices.text: Go to the eunuch and beg

ok.log: The eunuch is amused enough to have the sentence reduced to two years.

fail.log: The eunuch is not amused. Five years.

events.text: Willowford is still black in places: the mill, the granary and the row of houses you burned on a bad night long ago, when a debt went unpaid and you wanted the county to remember. Nettles grow through the old hearths. Children play in the ruins and stop when they see you.

choices.text: Start clearing the mill race with your own hands

effects.log: You dig out the mill race all spring. Nobody helps. Nobody stops you either.
A builder from the county town arrives with his sons and a cart of timber. (-200 taels)
You turn your horse before the first house. The children start playing again.

events.text: The village elder, Granny Shen, stands at the edge of your work with her arms crossed. The new mill wheel turns. 'A wheel does not give my son back his three years in the cold,' she says. 'But the children like it. Go on, then.' Half the village still will not speak to you.

effects.log: You raise the granary posts with the two men who will talk to you, and then with four.

choices.text: Ask Granny Shen what is needed most

ok.log: 'A school roof,' she says, 'and then the granary, and then go.' You do it in that order.

fail.log: She tells you to guess, and walks off. You guess wrong twice.

effects.log: You leave with the wheel turning. Granny Shen does not watch you go.

events.text: The last house is finished: new roof tiles, a carved door, a stove that draws. Granny Shen hands you the first bowl of rice from the new granary, then steps back. The whole village has come out to see what you do with it.

effects.log: You eat every grain. Granny Shen nods once. It is the most anyone in Willowford has ever said to you.
The children share it out, one grain at a time, very seriously. Even Granny Shen laughs.

choices.text: Bow and leave without a word

effects.log: You set the bowl down and walk out of Willowford. Behind you, someone starts the mill.

events.text: The Temple of the Listening Bell keeps a single old monk who hears what people cannot say elsewhere. You sit across from Master Kong in a bare room with one candle, and find that the list is longer than you thought when you set out.

effects.log: It takes until the candle is a stub. Master Kong does not interrupt once.
You tell the easier half. Master Kong listens to that, and to what you leave out.
You stand at the door a long time, then go. The candle is still burning when you look back.

events.text: Master Kong gives you no prayers to say. He gives you a list instead: a ferryman in Yichang, a widow in Nanyang, a ruined tea shop in Hangzhou, all names from your own mouth. 'Go and ask each one what is owed,' he says. 'Then come back.'

effects.log: It takes a year and most of your silver. Every door is different. (-150 taels)

choices.text: Go only to the ones who will not hate you

effects.log: You visit the ferryman and skip the widow. Master Kong does not ask, which tells you he knows.
Master Kong puts it in the poor box without looking at it, and hands you the list again. (-100 taels)

events.text: Master Kong sends a novice after you with a single line on a slip of paper: 'What you kept back is heavier than what you put down.' You find yourself thinking of it on the road, at meals, and in the middle of the night.

effects.log: You go back and tell the rest. It is worse than the first half and much lighter afterwards.
You keep it. The slip of paper stays in your sleeve for years.

events.text: You come back to the Temple of the Listening Bell with dust in your hair. The ferryman forgave you. The widow did not. The tea shop owner threw a pot at you and then made you tea. Master Kong listens to all of it and rings the bell, once.

effects.log: You sit with him until dark. Neither of you says anything. The bell keeps humming.
You ring the bell every dawn for a year. People come to the temple to see who the new ringer is, and go away thoughtful.

events.text: A swordsman of nineteen in clean blue robes blocks the road with a drawn blade. 'Bai Qing, disciple of the Righteous Sword Wen,' he announces, voice cracking. 'My master hunted you for ten years. I will finish it.' His stance is good. His feet are wrong.
events.arc: Bai Qing at the Broken Pine

choices.text: Disarm him and send him home

ok.log: His sword goes into a ditch. He goes after it, red to the ears.

fail.log: He cuts your sleeve before you take the sword. He will tell that story for years.

choices.text: Correct his feet and walk off

effects.log: You kick his back foot an inch to the left and walk on. He stands there a long time, feeling the difference.

choices.text: Humiliate him in front of the crowd

effects.log: You take his sword, his belt and his dignity. The crowd laughs. He does not.

events.text: Bai Qing is back, older and quieter, with a scar on his chin and a sword that does not shake. The Righteous Sword Wen is dead, and the disciple has come to the duel alone, at the Broken Pine at dawn, as the teahouses arranged without asking you.
events.arc: Bai Qing at the Broken Pine

ok.log: It is a long, clean fight. When his sword falls, he bows to you before he picks it up.

fail.log: His sword is at your throat. He lowers it, and walks away.

effects.log: He waits under the pine until noon. The teahouses decide you were afraid.
You let him win. He knows, and lets you go anyway.

events.text: Bai Qing has a small hall now, with eleven disciples, and the duel at the Broken Pine is the first story he tells them. In his telling the villain lost, and then he let the villain go, which is true. He sends a jar of plum wine and an invitation to watch them train.
events.arc: Bai Qing at the Broken Pine

effects.log: You sit at the back of his hall. His disciples have perfect feet.

choices.text: Correct his feet one last time

effects.log: You kick his back foot an inch to the left. Eleven disciples gasp. Bai Qing laughs until he cries.

events.text: Bai Qing did not come back after the Broken Pine. His hall closed. Then a letter, at last: he farms melons in Henan now, and his feet, he writes, have never been more correct. 'Thank you for ending a stupid thing. I would have kept at it until it ended me.'
events.arc: Bai Qing at the Broken Pine

effects.log: You eat melons on his porch until dark. Neither of you mentions swords.
He writes back that they grew enormous and he named the best one after you. (-20 taels)

events.text: Fat Dong and Thin Ma have stopped speaking. The argument is about which of them is your right hand, and it has reached the stage of separate cooking fires and a rope down the middle of the hideout. This morning Thin Ma moved the rope a foot to the left.

choices.text: Declare Fat Dong the right hand

effects.log: Fat Dong cooks a feast. Thin Ma eats none of it and moves the rope two feet.

choices.text: Declare both of them left hands

effects.log: They are so offended that they agree with each other for the first time in a year.
A race to the market and back with a basket of eggs. Both come back without eggs. (-10 taels)

events.text: The squabble has spread. The crew of eleven is now two factions with their own songs, and a cook who serves both and charges each extra. Last night someone stole the hideout's only kettle to make a point. You found out because you wanted tea.

ok.log: Two heads, one knock. The kettle reappears by morning, polished.

fail.log: They unite at once, in disliking you. The kettle stays missing.

choices.text: Take them on a job together

ok.log: Nothing makes friends like a shared escape over a wall. They sing the same song on the way home. (+120 taels)

fail.log: They argue in the middle of the job about who carries the bag. The constables carry it instead.

effects.log: Peace is restored, one kettle each. You still have no tea. (-10 taels)

events.text: Fat Dong and Thin Ma come to you together, which is new. They have agreed on one thing: that you should retire and let them run the crew. They have written it on paper, misspelled your name, and both signed it.

effects.log: You hand them the keys. They argue over your old chair for a week, and then both sit on it.
You frame the paper. They are both very hurt, together.
The crew dissolves in a month. You hear Fat Dong and Thin Ma opened a noodle shop, and argue in it daily.

events.text: The Kaifeng magistrate has a signed confession: you, it says, broke into the Prefect's summer house and took the jade horse of the Tang emperor. You were in Sichuan that month and have never seen a jade horse. The confession is in very good handwriting, much better than yours.

effects.log: You buy the confession from a yamen clerk and study the brushwork. It is a professional hand.
You let it stand. The teahouses say you stole a jade horse from under a Prefect's nose. You did not, and it is very good for business.
You ignore it. Everyone else does not.

events.text: The trail leads to a calligraphy shop by the Bian river and a gentle scholar called Teacher Yan, who forges confessions for a living and is mortified to meet you. 'It pays the rent,' he says. 'The client was the Prefect's own nephew. You were the obvious name.'

choices.text: Make Yan write the true confession

ok.log: He writes it in his best hand, trembling. It names the nephew and the pawnshop.

fail.log: He faints. When he wakes he has forgotten how to hold a brush, for now.

ok.log: You leave with the jade horse, which you have now actually stolen. (+150 taels)

fail.log: The nephew's guards are better than expected. Now there are two confessions.

choices.text: Pay Yan to forge something useful

effects.log: A pass for every city gate in Henan, in a magistrate's hand. (-40 taels)

events.text: Teacher Yan's true confession reaches the yamen, the Prefect's nephew is quietly posted to the frontier, and the magistrate has to strike your name off a charge for the first time in his career. He does it very slowly, as if hoping you will do something else in the meantime.

ok.log: He accepts your thanks through his teeth, and does not arrest you, because he cannot think of a reason fast enough.

fail.log: He thinks of a reason.

choices.text: Send Yan a brush of Huzhou hair

effects.log: He writes back in a beautiful hand that he has given up confessions for poetry. (-25 taels)
For one charge, at least, your name is clean.

events.text: Thirty years is a long time, but not long enough for Constable Ouyang, now white-haired and retired, who has kept one file open on his desk all that time: the Moon Bridge robbery, in which a young courier was hurt and never walked again. The file has your old name in it.

effects.log: He serves you tea in his garden and reads you the file, page by page, without raising his voice.
You go north. A month later a letter in Ouyang's hand finds you anyway.

choices.text: Send someone to steal the file

effects.log: The thief brings back the file. Ouyang, it turns out, has three copies. (-50 taels)

events.text: The courier from the Moon Bridge is alive. His name is Jiang, he is fifty-one, he weaves baskets in a wheeled chair outside Nanyang's east gate, and Constable Ouyang writes that Jiang has asked for one thing: to hear it from you.

effects.log: You go to Nanyang. The east gate is smaller than you remembered.
You write and rewrite it for a month. Ouyang carries it himself.
You burn the letter. Ouyang writes once more, and then never again.

events.text: Jiang listens to the whole story without stopping his hands. When you finish, he ties off a basket and puts it in your lap. 'I hated you for twenty years,' he says. 'Then I got tired. Carry this to the market for me. It is heavy.'

effects.log: You carry it to the market. You come back the next day, and the next, for a year.
He takes it for his nieces and gives you a second basket to carry. (-200 taels)

choices.text: Ask Ouyang to close the file with your confession

effects.log: Ouyang closes the file in front of you. The magistrate gives you two years, which Ouyang thinks is too few and Jiang thinks is too many.

events.text: Constable Ouyang dies in the winter, and the Moon Bridge file passes to a young constable who has never heard of you and puts it at the bottom of a pile. Somewhere outside Nanyang a basket-weaver keeps working. Nothing is closed. It just stops being opened.

effects.log: You light three sticks at his grave and stand there until they burn down.
Jiang is at the east gate. He looks at you, and keeps weaving, and you sit down beside him.
It is over, and you feel nothing but relief. That is its own kind of answer.

events.text: In every village for a hundred li, parents say your name at bedtime: 'Eat your greens or the Scourge will come.' You are at a noodle stall when a child refuses the greens, hears your name, looks straight at you, and asks whether you would like them instead.

effects.log: You eat them, solemnly. The child stares. The whole stall stares.
The child eats every green in the bowl. The grateful mother pays for your noodles. (+10 taels)

choices.text: Tell the child the Scourge is busy

effects.log: 'Busy doing what?' 'Eating other people's greens.' The child thinks about this for a long time.

events.text: The spring fair at Dengfeng has a new puppet: you, in red lacquer with eyebrows like thunderclouds, beaten every afternoon by a wooden orthodox hero to great cheers. The puppeteer, a cheerful man called Lao Feng, is making a fortune. He has no idea you are in the front row.

effects.log: You cheer loudest of anyone. Lao Feng bows to you specially.

choices.text: Go backstage and fix the eyebrows

effects.log: Lao Feng realises who you are halfway through, and keeps painting, very carefully.
Lao Feng pays at once and offers to make the eyebrows bigger. (+40 taels)

events.text: A delegation from Willow Creek arrives at your gate: the headman, three mothers and a goat. Their children have stopped believing in the Scourge, and bedtime has become chaos. They ask, very respectfully, whether you might walk through the village once a year looking dreadful.

effects.log: You walk through Willow Creek once a year in a black cloak. They pay in rice and the goat. (+30 taels)
You look dreadful in the street and then drink tea with the mothers. The children are confused for years.
Willow Creek bedtimes remain chaos. The goat stays with you anyway.

events.text: Lao Feng's puppet show has added a second act: the Scourge, defeated, sits down with the wooden hero and they share a bowl of noodles. You suggested it. The children like the second act better, and nobody can explain why.

effects.log: You never miss it. The noodles in the second act are real, and Lao Feng always saves you a bowl.
In the third act the Scourge opens a noodle shop. It is the most popular puppet show in Henan.

events.text: You have bought a tea farm in the hills above Hangzhou under another name: forty terraces, a house with a leaking roof and an old manager called Uncle Bao who talks to the bushes. Nobody here knows you. The first week you sleep with a blade under the pillow. The second week you do not.

effects.log: Uncle Bao teaches you to pluck two leaves and a bud. Your hands, which have done worse things, are very bad at it.

choices.text: Keep a hand in the old trade

effects.log: One job a season, far away, to keep the roof on. (+60 taels)
Two old soldiers patrol the terraces and mostly drink tea. (-60 taels)

events.text: Three strangers come up the terrace path at dusk with their hands under their coats: a debt from the old days, come to collect. Uncle Bao, holding a pruning knife, steps in front of you. He thinks they are tax collectors. He does not like tax collectors.

choices.text: Deal with them quietly behind the drying shed

ok.log: The fight behind the shed is short and quiet. Uncle Bao thinks the strangers left on their own.

fail.log: They leave, but so does a good deal of your health. Uncle Bao makes you a poultice of tea leaves.

effects.log: You pay. They count it on the terrace wall and go back down the path. (-120 taels)

ok.log: Uncle Bao lectures them about tax for an hour. They leave, thoroughly confused.

fail.log: Uncle Bao gets a black eye and you get the rest. The strangers leave with your silver box.

events.text: The first spring harvest from the terraces is small and very good. Uncle Bao names the tea 'Quiet Guest'. A buyer from Suzhou offers a price that makes the old trade look silly. Across the valley, though, a poster with an old face has gone up at the post station.

effects.log: You stay. The poster fades in the rain. Quiet Guest sells out in Suzhou. (+80 taels)

choices.text: Move on before the poster finds you

effects.log: You leave the farm to Uncle Bao and go west. He sends you a tin of Quiet Guest every spring.

choices.text: Go back to the trade one last time

effects.log: One last job. It is never the last. (+150 taels)

events.text: The ruined Temple of Ten Thousand Buddhas, at night. Torches ring the hill below: three hundred of them, the Alliance and the orthodox sects and anyone else who wanted to be there. Inside, nine of your people are sharpening blades and swearing to die with you. There is a goat track down the back.
events.arc: The Temple of Ten Thousand Buddhas

choices.text: Send them down the goat track and stay alone

effects.log: They argue. You win. They go down the track one by one, and you sit on the steps alone.
Ten of you behind a broken gate. The torches below do not move tonight.

choices.text: Take everyone down the goat track

ok.log: Ten shadows down a goat track in the dark. By dawn the three hundred are besieging an empty temple.

fail.log: The track is watched. You fight your way back up to the temple and bar the gate.

events.text: The siege has run all winter. The besiegers have built huts, a kitchen and a market below the hill; the temple has a well and a stubborn store of turnips. Tonight the Alliance Leader sends up an envoy under a flag of truce: walk out alone and unarmed, and the rest may go free.
events.arc: The Temple of Ten Thousand Buddhas

effects.log: You walk down the hill alone. Behind you, your people walk free, singing a song about turnips.

ok.log: You break through the market, the kitchen and the vanguard, and are gone into the northern hills by dawn.

fail.log: The breakout fails at the kitchen. You wake in an Alliance cell.

choices.text: Slip away alone, and let them find an empty temple

ok.log: In the morning the Alliance finds only turnips and an empty temple. Nobody ever agrees on how you got out.

fail.log: A sentry is eating a turnip behind a rock exactly where you come down.

events.text: Years later, in a market town where no one knows you, a storyteller is telling the siege of the Temple of Ten Thousand Buddhas. In his version you died on the steps with a blade in each hand, and three hundred torches went out at once. The crowd loves it. You buy a pear and listen to the end.
events.arc: The Temple of Ten Thousand Buddhas

effects.log: You eat the pear and walk away. You died on those steps. It is a good way to have died.
You stand up and tell the true ending. Half the crowd runs. The storyteller asks you to come back tomorrow.
You drop silver in his bowl. He bows to you without knowing why. (-10 taels)

events.text: Your new henchman, Lost Road Lu, is strong, loyal and cheerful, and has never once arrived where he was sent. You send him to stop a tax cart on the road out of Xi'an. Three weeks later a letter comes from Guangzhou: 'Arrived. No cart. Sea very big. Please advise.'

effects.log: You send the fare and a map. He comes home by way of Fujian. (-30 taels)

choices.text: Tell him to stay and scout the coast

effects.log: He writes every week from a different town, none of them on the coast.
You never hear from him again. Sometimes you wonder which sea he found.

events.text: Lu is back, from the wrong direction, with a cart. It is not the tax cart. It is a cart of medicine for a fever town in Hunan, whose driver was so grateful for an escort that he wept. Lu delivered it, then came home. The town has written you a letter of thanks.

effects.log: Lu glows for a week. The fever town sends you a pickled duck every new year.

choices.text: Sell the next medicine cart instead

effects.log: Lu does not understand why the next cart has to go to a market. He does it anyway, sadly. (+80 taels)

choices.text: Make him the crew's messenger to everywhere you never want to go

effects.log: Every message you send through Lu arrives somewhere useful by accident. It is uncanny.

events.text: The Alliance sent forty swordsmen to your hideout last week, following a map they took from Lu, who was caught drawing it. They arrived, after many days, at a pig farm in Anhui. The Alliance is furious. Lu is proud. You are, somehow, safer than you have been in years.

effects.log: Lu becomes Keeper of Maps. The Alliance now has three of his maps and has visited three pig farms.
Lu draws a map a month, and leaves them in teahouses. The murim starts calling you the Phantom.
He holds it upside down and thanks you with tears in his eyes. (-15 taels)

events.text: Someone is robbing grain barges on the Yangzi and leaving notes signed with your name, in a spelling you would never use. The teahouses are delighted. The river guilds are furious. Your name grows for work you did not do, and the impostor is clearly having fun.

effects.log: You follow the notes downriver, one barge at a time.
You let it grow. By the end of the year you are famous for nine robberies you never did.
You post a notice in your own hand. Nobody believes it, but the guilds keep it on file.

events.text: The impostor is a thin, giggling former boatman called Shrimp Gu, who has your old coat (from a pawnshop), your scowl (practised in a puddle) and none of your skill. When you find him, he is overjoyed. 'You came!' he says. 'Will you sign my coat?'

effects.log: Gu cries with joy and falls off the barge. You fish him out and start teaching.

choices.text: Hand him to the river guilds

effects.log: The guilds lock Gu in a grain hold for a season. He sends you a fan letter from inside.

choices.text: Make him give the grain back

ok.log: Gu returns every sack, sniffling. The guilds find their grain on their own docks one morning.

fail.log: He sells the grain instead and proudly gives you the silver. (+30 taels)

events.text: Shrimp Gu has improved. He still giggles, but he can climb a mast without falling off and take a barge without leaving a note. Last week, for the first time, someone recognised him as Shrimp Gu and not as you. He came back sulking. You have never seen anyone so disappointed to be famous.

choices.text: Tell him to make his own name

effects.log: Gu takes it very seriously and becomes the River Shrimp. Within a year the guilds fear him more than you.
There are two of you on the river now. The guilds hire twice the guards.

events.text: The river guilds have found out who returned their grain, and their headman has sent a barge of melons and a cautious note: they will stop paying hunters to find you, if you will stop letting people use your name on their river.

effects.log: You agree. The river is quiet that year, and the melons are excellent.

choices.text: Agree, and eat the melons with Gu

effects.log: Gu eats eleven. The guild headman, who came to watch, eats four.

events.text: In the town of Pingyao there is a lame watchman, Old Zhou, who lost his post and the use of one leg the night you robbed the Golden Abacus bank. You have come back with three hundred taels in a bag and a speech you have practised all the way from the river.

choices.text: Knock and give it to him yourself

effects.log: You knock. A long time passes before the door opens.
A noodle-seller next door agrees to carry it in for you. You wait across the street.

choices.text: Leave it on his step and go

effects.log: You leave the bag and walk away fast. You never learn what he did with it. (-300 taels)

events.text: Zhou opens the door, listens to half the speech and throws the bag into the street. 'You want me to say it is all right,' he says. 'It is not. I will not take your silver so you can sleep.' He shuts the door. Neighbours have gathered. They are all looking at you.

choices.text: Pick up the bag and go

effects.log: You pick up the silver from the street, coin by coin, while Pingyao watches.

choices.text: Sit down on his step and wait

effects.log: You sit on the step until dark. The door does not open.

choices.text: Give it to the watchmen's fund in his name

effects.log: The watch captain takes it and promises to tell no one whose silver it was. Zhou finds out anyway. (-300 taels)

events.text: You come back every week for a year and sit on the step. Zhou never opens the door. Once, in the cold, a bowl of millet is left on the step, which might be from him and might be from a neighbour. The town has started calling you the Step.

effects.log: He never opens the door. But he stops shouting through it, and one day the millet bowl has two spoons.

choices.text: Stop, and leave him in peace

effects.log: Some debts cannot be paid to the one you owe. You stop coming, and the step stays empty.

events.text: The noodle-seller brings back the silver, untouched, wrapped in a sheet of paper with one line in a shaky hand: 'Not for sale.' Pingyao's children follow you to the town gate, chanting a song about the Golden Abacus you did not know existed.

effects.log: You walk out of the gate with the song behind you. You will hear it in your sleep for a while.

choices.text: Give it to the town temple

effects.log: The temple takes it. The song goes on. (-300 taels)

events.text: The Orphan House of the Merciful Lotus in Yangzhou is falling down. The abbess, a sharp-eyed nun called Jingxin, takes your heavy purse, weighs it in her palm, and asks one question: 'Where did it come from?'

effects.log: She listens, nods, and keeps the purse. (-300 taels)
You say it is an inheritance. She keeps the purse and looks at you a moment too long. (-300 taels)
You take the purse back. The abbess does not look surprised.

events.text: The orphan house has a new roof, a well and a teacher. The children have no idea who paid. Then a magistrate's clerk arrives: the silver has been traced to the robbery of the Huai salt office, and the clerk wants it returned, roof or not.

choices.text: Take the blame so the house keeps it

effects.log: You walk into the yamen and confess. The roof stays. The children wave at your cart.

choices.text: Repay the salt office from somewhere else

effects.log: You pay the salt office out of your own pocket. The clerk is very confused. (-300 taels)
The roof stays, but the teacher goes. The children are back to learning from the nuns.

events.text: Abbess Jingxin writes in her severe hand: one of the orphans, a boy called Stone, has found out who paid for the roof and wants to meet the villain. 'I could not stop him,' she writes. 'I did not try very hard.'

effects.log: Stone asks you forty questions, most of them about swords and one about whether you are sorry. You answer that one first.
You write him a long letter. He writes back three pages, mostly drawings of you.

events.text: Abbess Jingxin knew all along. She tells you so at the gate, kindly enough. 'Lying to a nun is a small sin,' she says. 'Lying to yourself is the one that keeps you from sleep.' She does not give the silver back.

effects.log: You admit it. She nods, and gives you a bowl of the orphans' porridge, which is terrible.
You laugh. So does she, unexpectedly, and closes the gate.

events.text: Your old bookkeeper, Abacus Feng, kept a ledger of everything: every job, every bribe, every name. He retired to Suzhou with it, and now a note arrives in his neat hand. The Alliance has offered him 2,000 taels, and he would like to know if you can beat it.

effects.log: You send silver. Feng sends back a receipt, beautifully written. (-300 taels)

choices.text: Go to Suzhou and take the ledger

ok.log: You take it from under his pillow while he snores. He has, of course, already made a note of it.

fail.log: Feng's nephews are awake. You leave without the ledger, and with a bruise.

effects.log: He sells it. You hear the Alliance Leader stayed up three nights reading.

events.text: The ledger sits on your table: forty years of your life in Feng's tidy columns. Read one way it is evidence. Read another, it is a list of everyone you have wronged, with their towns and the exact amounts.

effects.log: It burns slowly, page by page. The past is ash, or at least smoke.

choices.text: Use it to pay people back

effects.log: You start at the first page. It takes a year to reach the tenth. (-200 taels)

choices.text: Use it to squeeze your old clients

effects.log: Everyone who ever paid you to do something has a reason to pay you again. (+250 taels)

events.text: The Alliance has your ledger, and is reading it aloud: in a public hall in Luoyang, a scribe reads one page every day, and people come to hear their own names. Some come because you robbed them. Some come because they paid you to rob someone else.

effects.log: You sit in the back for a week. You had forgotten most of it. They had not.

ok.log: The ledger vanishes from the hall. The Alliance has the first forty pages copied, and no more.

fail.log: The scribe is a better guard than he looks.

effects.log: The reading goes on for a year. It becomes the most popular entertainment in Luoyang.

events.text: Abacus Feng writes again, in the same neat hand. The Alliance has raised its offer to 3,000 taels, and his roof needs mending. He encloses an itemised bill for the roof, with the tiles counted to the last one.

effects.log: You pay for every tile. The receipt is a work of art. (-80 taels)

ok.log: You drink tea all afternoon. He hands you the ledger at the door. 'I only wanted company,' he says.

fail.log: He enjoys the visit very much and sells the ledger the next day.

events.text: Old Master Tan of Mask Lane in Chengdu makes opera masks, and for 60 taels he will make you one the whole murim will remember: black lacquer, gold brows, a mouth like a split pomegranate. 'A face for the posters,' he says. 'Better than the one you were born with.'

effects.log: It fits like a second skin. The first person who sees you in it drops a teapot. (-60 taels)
He makes you a plain grey mask with a sigh of deep disappointment. (-20 taels)
Tan shrugs. 'Your loss,' he says, and goes back to his brushes.

events.text: The mask has caught on. Every bandit from here to Kunming wears a cheap copy, the opera troupes have added it to their stock, and children wear paper ones at the Duanwu festival. Last week three different people in your mask were arrested on the same day.

effects.log: Tan makes you a new one, silver brows this time. Within a month there are copies of that too. (-60 taels)
Nobody looks at your face any more. They are all looking at masks.

choices.text: Ask Master Tan for a share

effects.log: Tan laughs and pays. He has sold two thousand copies. (+100 taels)

events.text: Master Tan sends a note: the Sichuan governor has banned the mask, and the yamen has shut his shop. He is seventy-four and has no other trade. His apprentice, who painted the gold brows, has been taken in for questioning.

ok.log: You talk the yamen into letting the apprentice go, and the shop opens again, selling fans.

fail.log: The yamen keeps the apprentice, and you as well, for a year.

effects.log: Tan reopens and makes only opera masks after that, very respectable ones. (-100 taels)
Mask Lane loses one shop. The governor keeps the masks, and wears one at home.

events.text: The wound in your side has gone bad, and the only physician within three days' walk is Doctor Song of the Benevolent Hall, an orthodox healer whose cousin you robbed. You stagger in at midnight. Song looks at the wound, then at your face, and puts the kettle on.

effects.log: Song stitches it without a word, and gives you a bed by the stove.

choices.text: Hold a blade to Song while being treated

effects.log: Song stitches it with your blade at the back of the neck, and the stitches are perfect.

ok.log: You clean it yourself in a barn with rice wine and herbs. It heals, slowly.

fail.log: It goes worse before it goes better. You lose a month and something more.

events.text: Doctor Song's message comes on a slip of red paper: plague in the county below the Benevolent Hall, and the orthodox sects will not send people into it. 'You owe me a stitch,' it says. 'I am collecting it.'

ok.log: You carry the sick for a season, two at a time. Song works beside you and does not say thank you once.

fail.log: You fall sick yourself in the second month. Song treats you again, grumbling.

effects.log: Song sends back a receipt and nothing else. (-120 taels)
You burn the red slip. The plague passes without you.

events.text: The plague has passed. Doctor Song's cousin, the one you robbed, comes to the Benevolent Hall to thank the stranger who carried his children down the hill, and stops in the doorway when he sees your face. Song is pretending to be very busy with a mortar.

effects.log: The cousin listens, then sits down heavily. "Well," he says. "You carried them." It is not forgiveness, but it is close.
You bow to him like a stranger. He bows back like one. Song grinds the mortar louder.
He takes it, and gives half of it to Song for the Hall. (-100 taels)

events.text: Doctor Song never reported you. Instead a small package arrives: a jar of wound salve and a note. 'For next time. Please do not bring a blade into my hall again; it frightens the apprentices.'

effects.log: You write the most careful letter of your life. Song writes back two words: "Accepted. Salve."
It is very good salve. You use it more often than you would like.

events.text: A tap at the window at night: Turtle Sun, who shared a cell with you and taught you to play go with pebbles. He is out now, and thin, and has a plan, which he whispers through the half-open shutter: the prison's pay chest, which the warden keeps under his bed.

effects.log: You shake on it through the window, the way you used to through the bars.

choices.text: Give him silver and send him off

effects.log: He looks at the silver a long time, then takes it and goes. (-50 taels)
You shut it. The tapping stops after a while.

events.text: The night of the job. The warden, it turns out, sleeps beside the pay chest with his grandson, who has a fever, and a nurse who has dozed off in her chair. Turtle Sun is already working at the lock with a spoon he has been sharpening since the first day of his sentence.

effects.log: The lock gives. You and Sun split the chest under a bridge at dawn. (+120 taels)
You take the spoon out of his hand. He looks at the boy for a long time, then follows you out.

choices.text: Wake the nurse for the boy and walk out

effects.log: The nurse wakes and runs for cold water. The warden never reports the open window.

events.text: Turtle Sun writes from Wuhan: with your silver he bought a cart and sells roast chestnuts below the Yellow Crane Tower. He has saved enough to send some back, which he does, with a bag of chestnuts and a go problem he says you will never solve.

ok.log: You solve it in a week and send back the answer. He writes that you cheated.

fail.log: You cannot solve it. He sends the answer with a drawing of a laughing turtle.

effects.log: You keep it and eat the chestnuts. (+30 taels)

choices.text: Send the silver back to him

effects.log: You send it back with a note: for the second cart.

events.text: Magistrate Kou of Linqing is fat, frightened and very corrupt, and he has invited you to dinner. Over eel and wine he offers you a post: unofficial enforcer of the county, paid from the tax chest, with all charges against you 'mislaid' while you serve.

effects.log: Kou pours you more tea and pushes a purse across the table. (+100 taels)

choices.text: Take it, and keep notes on him

effects.log: You take the purse and, that night, start a little book about Magistrate Kou. (+100 taels)
You leave the eel half eaten. Kou looks more frightened than before.

events.text: Kou's orders arrive on scented paper. This month: frighten a schoolteacher who wrote a poem about the magistrate's waistline, and collect a fish tax from the river families that the court abolished two years ago.

effects.log: The schoolteacher stops writing poems. The fishing families pay. (+80 taels)

choices.text: Frighten nobody, collect from the rich

ok.log: You collect the fish tax from Kou's own friends. They pay without understanding why. (+80 taels)

fail.log: Kou's friends complain to Kou. Kou complains to you, nervously.

effects.log: You send back the scented paper unread. Kou does not write again for a while.

events.text: The censor from the capital is coming to Linqing, and Magistrate Kou is in a panic. He needs someone to blame for the missing tax silver, and he has already chosen. The constables are on their way to your door, and Kou's own accounts are in his study.

choices.text: Take Kou's accounts to the censor

ok.log: The censor reads them in one sitting. Kou is stripped of his post, and your name is not in the report.

fail.log: You are caught in the study with the accounts in your hands, which looks very bad.

effects.log: You go north before the constables knock. Kou blames you anyway, in your absence.

ok.log: The constables go home. Kou finds someone else to blame and pays you to forget it. (+100 taels)

fail.log: There were more constables than you thought.

events.text: Years ago you took the Autumn Water sword from the Hengshan sect's hall, mostly to prove you could. Now the teahouses say it is cursed: three owners struck down, a flood, a fire. None of that is true. But Hengshan's elders have started visiting the teahouses and listening.

effects.log: You hang it over the bed. Visitors stop sitting near it.

ok.log: The sword is back on its rack by dawn. Hengshan announces a miracle.

fail.log: You are caught breaking into the hall to give something back, which nobody believes.

effects.log: A salt merchant from Yangzhou pays without haggling. (+300 taels)
