effects.log: The settling takes a season and leaves a crack in the sect that will need years of mending.

events.text: By the Cult's oldest law, a contested throne is climbed: ten thousand steps cut in the cliff of the Heavenly Demon's peak, and whoever reaches the throne first sits on it. The sibling who contests the seat starts at dawn.
events.arc: Ten Thousand Steps to the Throne

choices.text: Start at dawn too and race.

ok.log: By the five-thousandth step you are ahead, and the wind is screaming in your ears.

fail.log: By the five-thousandth step your legs are lead and the other climber is a speck above you.

choices.text: Start at noon, slowly, saving your breath.

effects.log: The cultists on the cliff hoot at you. The steps do not care.

choices.text: Bribe the gatekeepers to bar the sibling's path for an hour (-100 taels).

effects.log: The gate jams for an hour at step two thousand. You are far ahead by the time it opens. (-100 taels)

events.text: At the nine-thousandth step, there is a ledge, and on it, the sibling who contests the seat, sitting with a twisted ankle and a face like thunder. A thousand steps above, the throne.
events.arc: Ten Thousand Steps to the Throne

effects.log: You reach the throne at sunset, alone. The Cult roars. The Cult respects exactly this.

choices.text: Carry the sibling the last thousand steps.

ok.log: You reach the throne with a rival on your back. By the old law the first feet on the dais win. Yours are.

fail.log: You fall short. The sibling hops the last step and sits. 'Thank you,' they say, and mean it, and take the throne.

choices.text: Sit down beside them and wait for the healers.

effects.log: The healers come at dusk. By then, a third claimant has reached the top, and you both laugh until it hurts. You give up the throne.

events.text: At the nine-thousandth step you look down: the sibling who contests the seat is a thousand steps below and climbing hard. A thousand steps above, the throne. The wind drops, and for a moment it is very quiet.
events.arc: Ten Thousand Steps to the Throne

effects.log: You reach the throne at dusk and sit. The Cult kneels, and the one who came second kneels last.

choices.text: Wait at the top step, and face your rival in a duel for it.

roll.foeName: the sibling who contests the seat

ok.log: Before the throne, before the whole Cult, you win it twice: by the steps and by the fist.

fail.log: You lose the duel on the last step. By the old law, you yield the throne.

events.text: The Imperial Jade Seal has vanished from the Hall of Preserving Harmony. Without it, no edict of yours is law. The sibling who contests the seat says nothing, which in the palace is a kind of shouting.

ok.log: The seat-keeper, Eunuch Bao, cannot meet your eyes. Under his bed, in a rice jar: the seal.

fail.log: Every eunuch's bed is overturned, and the palace learns to hate you a little.

choices.text: Have a new seal carved in secret (-200 taels).

effects.log: The carver is the best in the capital and swears silence on his grandchildren. (-200 taels)

choices.text: Rule without a seal. Let the court see what you do, not what you stamp.

effects.log: Your edicts go out signed in your own hand. The provinces are puzzled, then oddly impressed.

events.text: Censor Lu Wenyi rises at morning court with a memorial a yard long. The question is simple and fatal: by what seal does this throne rule? Every minister turns to look at the empty cushion where the seal should sit.

choices.text: Lift the true seal before the court.

effects.log: Eunuch Bao is led away weeping. The court kneels as one. The throne is yours, sealed.

choices.text: Pardon Eunuch Bao in front of the court, and ask who paid him.

effects.log: Eunuch Bao looks at the sibling who contests the seat. So does everyone. That is the end of the contest.

events.text: Censor Lu Wenyi rises at morning court with a memorial a yard long: by what seal does this throne rule? On the cushion beside you sits a seal of new jade, still faintly warm from the carver's polishing cloth.

choices.text: Lift the new seal and dare the court to doubt it.

ok.log: The court bows to a lie of the finest jade. You win, and you will never be sure who knows.

fail.log: The censor holds up the true seal, found that morning. The throne passes to the sibling who contests it.

choices.text: Confess the copy, and ask the court to judge by deeds.

effects.log: The court is stunned. The contest drags on another season, but the censor tips his hat.

events.text: Censor Lu Wenyi rises with his yard-long memorial, and then, unexpectedly, reads out a list: your edicts of the year, signed by hand. Rice prices down, two floods managed, a war not started. The sibling who contests the seat listens with folded hands.

effects.log: 'A seal is a stone,' the censor says. 'This is a ruler.' The court kneels. Days later the true seal turns up in a eunuch's rice jar.

choices.text: Step down rather than split the empire.

effects.log: You give up the Dragon Throne before the court, by your own hand, and leave the palace by the east gate.

events.text: The house's whole fortune is a noodle stall at the East Gate and a broth recipe nobody has ever written down. The sibling who contests the seat says the head is whoever makes the better broth. The street has already heard.

choices.text: Accept. Cook-off at the stall, the street as judge.

effects.log: Within a day, the whole street is arguing about who will win. Business doubles.

choices.text: Go to old Granny Chu, who cooked for the house forty years.

effects.log: She tells you one secret: a dried tangerine peel, and patience. Then she falls asleep.

choices.text: Refuse. The seat is not soup.

effects.log: The street boos you all the way home.

events.text: The day of the broth. Two pots, one stall, a crowd of porters, three monks and a magistrate's clerk who came for lunch and stayed to judge. Steam rises.

choices.text: Cook it the way you remember from childhood.

ok.log: The clerk takes one sip and closes his eyes. The porters cheer. The stall is yours.

fail.log: Your broth is good. The other pot is better. You hand over the ladle and the seat.

choices.text: Add Granny Chu's tangerine peel, and wait.

ok.log: The first spoonful tastes like your grandparents' kitchen. The crowd goes quiet. The seat is yours.

fail.log: You wait too long and the peel turns bitter. The clerk calls it a draw and orders seconds.

choices.text: Pour both pots into one and serve it to everyone.

effects.log: The mixed broth is the best ever made at the East Gate. The contest is off for another year.

events.text: You won the seat, but four elders voted against you, and they sit in the hall each morning like four black stones in the bronze bowl. Elder Rao, the eldest of them, has stopped coming to the morning practice.

choices.text: Visit Elder Rao at his pavilion with tea.

effects.log: He receives you coldly and keeps you for three hours, telling you everything you do wrong.

choices.text: Give each of the four a hall of their own to run.

effects.log: Four black stones, four busy halls. Less time for grumbling, more for work.

choices.text: Retire the four with honours and gifts (-150 taels).

effects.log: The four leave the mountain. The sect is quieter and a little smaller. (-150 taels)

events.text: A rival sect raids the sect's herb gardens in the lower valley. The four elders who voted against you are the first in the hall, swords drawn, waiting to see what you will do.

ok.log: The raiders are driven out by sunset. Elder Rao fights at your shoulder and says nothing, which is high praise.

fail.log: You are wounded, and the four elders finish the fight. They bring you back on a door.

effects.log: Elder Rao takes the command, wins, and comes back to the hall carrying a white stone, which he drops in the bowl at your feet.

events.text: At the founder's anniversary, the nine elders vote again, by old custom, on whether the seat is well held. Elder Qiu brings the bronze bowl to the dais.

ok.log: Nine white stones. Elder Rao's is the first in the bowl.

fail.log: Eight white, one black. The black stone is Elder Rao's, and he winks as he drops it.

choices.text: Tell them the old custom is over. The seat answers to the whole sect now.

effects.log: The elders are startled. The disciples love it. You have made a new custom, which is harder.

events.text: The seat is gone. You leave with a bundle, a little silver, and the eyes of the whole house on your back. At the ferry crossing, the boatman asks where to, and for the first time in years nobody else is answering for you.

choices.text: South, to Jiangnan, where nobody knows the house.

effects.log: The boat goes south. The river is wide and does not ask questions.

choices.text: Stay at the ferry and help the boatman for a while.

effects.log: The boatman is old and his back is bad. You pull the rope. He pays in fish.

choices.text: Go back to the house and ask for a place under the new head.

effects.log: You are given a small room by the kitchen. Everyone is very polite, which is the worst of it.

events.text: A year on. The ferry has a second boat now, and a teahouse on the landing where travellers wait for it, and both of them are, somehow, yours. The boatman is thinking of retiring.

choices.text: Buy the ferry from him (-120 taels).

effects.log: The boatman retires to his daughter's house. The ferry is the first thing you have ever owned outright. (-120 taels)

choices.text: Keep working it as his partner.

effects.log: Half the fares and all the gossip of the river. (+40 taels)

events.text: In Jiangnan you rent a room above a silk shop and do whatever needs doing: accounts, letters, once a funeral. Slowly a name forms, and it is yours, not the house's.

choices.text: Open a small counting house of your own (-80 taels).

effects.log: The sign over the door has your name on it and nobody else's. (-80 taels)

choices.text: Keep doing a little of everything.

effects.log: Every street in the quarter knows you. You have never been so poor or so free.

events.text: The new head of the house has given you the kitchen room, a stipend, and nothing to do. The servants call you 'the other one'. A cousin is getting married; you are seated near the door.

choices.text: Leave after the wedding and do not come back.

effects.log: You walk out of the gate with the wedding music still playing. The road feels better than the room.

choices.text: Make yourself useful until you are needed.

effects.log: Within two years you are running the granary, and the new head asks your opinion before anyone else's.

events.text: Years later, a messenger from the old house finds you, out of breath. The house wants you back, at a high table, with honour. Someone has finally remembered what you were good at.

effects.log: You go back for a season, fix what needs fixing, and leave again. Nobody seats you near the door. (+80 taels)

choices.text: Send the messenger back with a gift and a no.

effects.log: The no is gentle. What you have built is yours, and it does not need a seat.

events.text: The clan seal, carved from a single piece of mutton-fat jade in the Tang dynasty, is gone from its box. Without it, no land deed of the clan can be signed. Three people had the key: Cousin Rong, Steward Mei and you.

ok.log: Cousin Rong is sweating, but over a betrothal gift sold to a jeweller. Not the seal. But you learn something.

fail.log: Cousin Rong storms off to complain to the elders, loudly.

effects.log: Steward Mei quietly hands you a list: every time the box was opened in thirty years, and by whom. One date is wrong.

choices.text: Announce the loss to the whole clan.

effects.log: The clan is in uproar. Somewhere in the uproar, someone is very relieved.

events.text: Steward Mei's list shows the box was opened at the last Mid-Autumn feast, by the head before you, who has been dead three years. Either a ghost has the key, or the seal was moved long ago and the box has been empty all along.

ok.log: Inside a hollow inkstone, wrapped in silk: the seal, and a note: 'Hidden from bandits. Tell the heir.' Nobody did.

fail.log: Dust, poems and a very old pear. The seal is not there.

choices.text: Have a new seal carved and say nothing (-150 taels).

effects.log: The new seal is beautiful and wrong in a way only the dead would notice. (-150 taels)

events.text: Without the seal, Cousin Rong has started calling the clan's deeds unsigned and the clan's head unproven. Some of the younger cousins are listening, and the magistrate has sent back two deeds unread.

choices.text: Call the clan together and sign every new deed with your own red thumbprint.

effects.log: The cousins grumble, but the deeds hold in the magistrate's court. A seal, it turns out, is only a habit.

choices.text: Offer a reward for the seal (-50 taels).

effects.log: A month later, the old head's maid finds it in a hollow inkstone and is paid. The clan relaxes. (-50 taels)

events.text: You give each of your grown children the same thing: one hundred taels and one year. 'Show me what a head of this house would do with it,' you say. The ledgers will tell you the rest.

effects.log: The silver goes out of the strongbox in neat stacks, one hundred per child. (-100 taels)

choices.text: Give them the silver, and do not watch at all.

effects.log: You go fishing for a year. It is the best year of your life. (-100 taels)

choices.text: Give them nothing but the order: 'Find your own hundred.'

effects.log: There is a lot of grumbling. Then there is a lot of work.

events.text: A year later the results are on the table. One child has turned a hundred into four hundred, selling tea to the army. Another has two hundred, and a reputation for fair weights. A third spent it all on a well in a dry village.

choices.text: Name the one with four hundred.

ok.log: The tea trader takes the house and its silver, and runs both hard. (+150 taels)

fail.log: The army contracts were not quite honest. The house is named to the sharpest child anyway. (+50 taels)

choices.text: Hold a fair trial between the honest trader and the well-digger.

effects.log: The trial is long and the merchants' guild watches it. The new heir is named, and the guild approves.

choices.text: Keep the house yourself a few years more, and visit the dry village.

effects.log: The well is deep and the water sweet. The villagers want to know if the house sells anything they could buy.

events.text: The guild hall holds a dinner for heads of merchant houses. For the first time your heir sits at your right, and the old men are watching to see who pours the wine.

effects.log: The heir pours, toasts and talks prices like a veteran. The old men nod and look at you differently: as someone's elder.

choices.text: Pour it yourself, one last time.

effects.log: Your hand is a little slow. Nobody minds. It is the best wine of the year.

events.text: A fever takes you in the winter, and the physician from Willow Lane shakes his head over your pulse. By the third day your grown children are all in the house, and there is a great deal of whispering in the corridor.

choices.text: Listen to the whispering with your eyes closed.

effects.log: You learn who wants the seal, who wants the pear orchard, and who just wants you to live.

choices.text: Send everyone away and call for a better physician (-60 taels).

effects.log: The second physician is ruder and much better. You are sitting up in a week. (-60 taels)

choices.text: Ask for paper and write a will while you still can.

effects.log: Your hand shakes. You write three lines and seal them, and do not say what they are.

events.text: You recover. The whole house is overjoyed, or at least says so. At the spring feast, you sit at the head of the table and look at each of them in turn, remembering the corridor.

choices.text: Say nothing, but give the pear orchard to the one who only wanted you to live.

effects.log: The others are puzzled, then embarrassed, then very attentive for years.

choices.text: Tell them, kindly, everything you heard.

effects.log: There is a terrible silence, and then one by one they laugh. The house is closer for it, somehow.

choices.text: Hold a trial for the heir now, while you are well enough to judge it.

effects.log: Better a trial at a feast than a quarrel at a coffin. The heir is named before the tablets.

events.text: You recover, and the sealed will is still in the box by your bed. Everyone has noticed it. Nobody mentions it. The house has never been so well-behaved.

choices.text: Open it before them all. It says: 'Be kind to each other. I am watching.'

effects.log: They laugh until they cry. The will goes back in the box for the next fever.

choices.text: Leave it sealed and enjoy the good behaviour.

effects.log: It is a very pleasant few years.

events.text: The portrait of the head before you hangs in the hall, painted in the last year of their life. Old retainers bow to it on their way to you. Twice this month, someone has said, 'In the old head's time, we did it differently.'

choices.text: Ask them how it was done differently.

effects.log: Most of it is nostalgia. One thing in ten is wisdom. You write that one down.

choices.text: Move the portrait to the ancestral hall, with the tablets.

effects.log: The hall looks empty without it. The retainers look at you instead.

choices.text: Have your own portrait painted to hang beside it (-50 taels).

effects.log: The painter flatters you a little and the old head a lot. (-50 taels)

events.text: A crisis: the river rises, and the house must decide in an hour whether to open the dykes onto its own fields to save the village. The old retainers look at the portrait, and then at you.

effects.log: The fields drown and the village lives. (-100 taels)

choices.text: Hold the dykes and send boats to the village.

ok.log: The boats get everyone out and the fields survive. The retainers have never seen it done.

fail.log: The boats are too few and too late. Two houses are lost. The village does not forget.

events.text: The oldest retainer, Uncle Gao, comes to you with a key. 'The old head opened the dykes too, in the year I was young,' he says. 'And left this for whoever did it next.' The key opens a box of seed grain, kept dry for thirty years.

choices.text: Plant it on the drowned fields.

effects.log: The old seed comes up thick and gold. The house is not poor for long. (+120 taels)

choices.text: Give it to the village to plant.

effects.log: The village plants it, and the next year brings you the first sheaf. They hang it under the portrait.

events.text: A man calling himself Prince Rui has appeared in the south, claiming to be the true heir, smuggled out of the palace as a baby during the last rebellion. He has a birthmark, a jade pendant and three provinces cheering him.

choices.text: Have the old palace nurses questioned.

ok.log: Nurse Ji, ninety-one, laughs until she coughs. 'That pendant was sold in the market for fourteen taels the year the palace burned.'

fail.log: Three nurses, three stories. Nobody knows anything for sure.

choices.text: Invite Prince Rui to the capital as a guest.

effects.log: He accepts, to everyone's surprise. He arrives with three hundred retainers and very good manners.

ok.log: The pretender's army breaks at the river. Prince Rui escapes into the hills, and the story with him.

fail.log: The army is stopped at the river, and the south cheers louder.

events.text: Prince Rui stands before the throne and the whole court. He is calm, charming, and wrong; the pendant is a market piece and everyone in the room now knows it. He knows it too.

choices.text: Have him exiled to the far west.

effects.log: He goes west with a bow, and is last heard of selling pendants in Dunhuang.

choices.text: Pardon him and make him a minor official in the south.

effects.log: The south loves the pardon more than it loved the prince. Prince Rui turns out to be a very good tax collector.
The example is made. Nobody claims a birthmark again for fifty years.

events.text: Prince Rui, or whoever he is, still holds the south's heart. The court whispers, and the whispers ask: what if he is real? In the south, temples have started lighting incense for his long life.

choices.text: Meet him in secret, alone, by the river.

effects.log: He tells you who he really is: an orphan of the rebellion, nothing more. He asks for a pardon for his followers and gets it.

choices.text: Lower the south's taxes for three years.

effects.log: The south forgets its prince within a year. Silver is louder than birthmarks. (-200 taels)

events.text: Aunt Shu of the West Courtyard branch comes to the main hall with eleven cousins behind her. 'We have been the clan's poor relations for three generations,' she says. 'Give us our share of the land, and our own tablets.'

choices.text: Hear the full case, with the land registers open.

effects.log: The registers prove her right. Her great-grandfather's fields were folded into the main line by a forged deed.

choices.text: Refuse. A clan divided is a clan finished.

effects.log: Aunt Shu leaves without bowing. The West Courtyard's gate is shut that night.

choices.text: Offer silver instead of land (-100 taels).

effects.log: The silver is taken, but Aunt Shu says it is a beginning, not an end. (-100 taels)

events.text: The register is wrong and Aunt Shu is right. Returning the land means the clan loses its best orchard. The elders are against it to a man, and Aunt Shu is waiting in the courtyard in the rain.

choices.text: Return the land, and help them set up their own tablets.

effects.log: The West Courtyard holds its first rites under its own roof. Aunt Shu bows to you, deeply. (-60 taels)

choices.text: Return half, and keep them in the clan.

effects.log: Half the orchard and a seat on the council. Nobody gets everything, so it holds.

events.text: A year of a shut gate. The West Courtyard branch has gone to the magistrate, and the magistrate has ordered the registers brought to his yamen by the next full moon. Aunt Shu has hired a famous pleader from the capital.

choices.text: Bring them, and accept what he finds.

effects.log: The magistrate finds the old forgery and returns the orchard to the West Courtyard. The gate opens again.

choices.text: Pay the magistrate's clerk to lose the registers (-80 taels).

effects.log: The registers are lost. So is any chance of peace with the West Courtyard. (-80 taels)
